correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the fixed Pappus LCF graph and verified all 18 BFS distance rows, its diameter 4, 27 edges, bipartition, and six disjoint distance-four triples. The radius-two pure-side subgraphs are each K_{3,3,3}; the two mixed cone covers retract to joins D3*D3*D3, intersect in G, and are simply connected. The null-attached homotopy pushout is (8+8+10)=26 copies of S2. Radius three is the join of six D3 giving 64 copies of S5. Radius one is a rank-10 graph and radius four a simplex. Exhaustive simplex enumeration and mod-two boundary ranks independently agree. There is no finite-to-infinite extrapolation: the claim is the fixed finite graph.

originality.rationale: The inspected graph-power, bipartite-square, circular-Rips and projective-plane incidence theorems provide relevant methods but do not give the Pappus graph full five-phase homotopy classification or its exact multiplicities 10, 26, 64. Kawamura 2011 is a substantive full-text comparison: it proves relative homological equivalence criteria and Dowker-Mather collapses, without computing these Pappus invariants. Adamaszek 2011 girth-collapse criterion requires girth at least 7 at radius 2, while Pappus girth is 6. The 2026 projective-plane incidence result assumes every two points share a line and has diameter 3, while the Pappus graph has diameter 4 and six distance-four triples. The public Pappus matching-complex calculation concerns a different simplicial complex. Unindexed equivalent computation remains a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, preprint, lecture note or database may already contain an equivalent Pappus graph-metric Rips filtration.

The full text of the Larrión–Pizaña–Villarroel-Flores 2009 paper was not available in the inspected source; its stated abstract addresses π1, so a concealed higher-dimensional explicit Pappus example cannot be absolutely excluded.
General bipartite-square arguments may permit alternative derivations of the scale-two result, but the checked sources do not supply the metric-specific computations or full barcode.

value.rationale: The Pappus graph is a canonical symmetric cubic incidence/distance-regular graph. Its complete all-scale Rips homotopy and persistence identify a natural, motivated structural distinction between projective-plane incidence systems and partial Pappus configurations. The explicitly explained 26 two-spheres and 64 five-spheres, integral torsion-freeness, and exact field-independent barcode go beyond Euler characteristics, isolated Betti-number checks or simple connectivity. This finite classification serves as a reproducible benchmark for incidence-geometry graph power topology.
